rule.description: A free analysis-entrypoint function whose nesting-aware cognitive complexity meets or exceeds the threshold has absorbed subordinate pipeline stages (collection, gating, sorting, and summarization) into one deeply-inlined body and should be re-extracted into focused helpers.

checks.description: The Dylint lint DEEPLY_INLINED_METHOD scores a Sonar-style cognitive complexity for every free, named function: each branch, match, or loop contributes 1 plus the current nesting, and each short-circuit && / || contributes 1. A function at or above the threshold signals that distinct responsibilities have been inlined into one body.
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The entrypoint no longer delegates collecting inputs, gating them, and summarizing results to focused helpers; each stage's control flow is absorbed in place, erasing the abstraction boundaries a maintainer must restore to reason about the analysis.

matches.evidence: `monos` folds generic-instantiation collection with deduplication and size sorting, per-generic total/bloat computation, per-options truncation of the retained instantiations, and the trailing entry-summary and totals rows into one body (cognitive complexity 92, threshold 40).

`dominators` folds the dominator-item selection together with a reachability DFS from the meta root and the unreachable-items summary that previously lived in a helper plus a cross-file `garbage` analysis (cognitive complexity 60, threshold 40).

`paths` folds the starting-position resolver, which was four sub-closures (regex match, exact-name match, default ascending, default descending) plus their option-driven dispatch, directly into the entrypoint (cognitive complexity 45, threshold 40).

excluded.reason: Trait-impl formatting methods (Display::fmt, Emit::emit_text/emit_json/emit_csv) and the recursive walk helpers perform a single formatting/walk responsibility rather than collapsed orchestration. The rule intentionally scopes to free, named functions and does not flag those method bodies, so emitted-format code is outside the rule.
